answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a stake-weighted identity registry: to join, each agent locks a refundable deposit of tokens, so creating an island of fake identities costs real capital per identity instead of being free. Attestations are then weighted by stake, and a sable-blacklist of proven misbehavior triggers slashing of the deposit. An attacker facing an ocean of honest, staked agents must outspend the entire honest stake to sway a vote, and every detected Sybil burns its deposit, so the attack's cost grows linearly with each fake identity while honest participation stays cheap.
